t: And at that moment he turned north and set off on a steady run to the north; and as he swam he met dozens of comrades, all hastening toward the same goal, and all of them hailed him: »Good luck, pup!

t: The sea on summer nights is full of fire over its whole expanse from Novastosna to Lukannon, and every sea lion leaves behind a streak as if of burning oil, and if he leaps, a flame flashes and the waves shatter into long phosphorescent streaks and circles.

o: Pak odebrali se na souš, na místa holušíků, a váleli se sem a tam po mladé divoké pšenici a vyprávěli si celé historie o tom, co vykonali, když byli v moři.
t: Then they went ashore, to where the boys were, and rolled about here and there in the young wild wheat, telling each other whole histories of what they had done at sea.

t: They talked about the Pacific as boys talk about a forest they have ranged in, and anyone who understood them could, from their accounts, have drawn a map of a sea that no one had yet charted.

t: "Look here, you young rascal, where did you get this white coat?"

t: "I didn't get it," answered Kotík, "it grew on me." And just as he was getting ready to knock the speaker down, a pair of black-haired men with flat, ruddy faces came out from behind a sandy dune, and Kotík, who had never yet seen a man, coughed and bowed his head.

o: Holušíkové odhopkovali tak několik kroků a usedli, hledíce hloupě a vyjeveně.

o: Přišli z malé vesnice, vzdálené sotva půl míle od lachtaních hnízdišť, a vyhlíželi, které lachtany mají odehnati k porážkovým ohradám; neboť lachtani byli honěni jako ovce, aby byli později opracováni v tulení – sealskinové – kožíšky.
t: They had come from a small village scarcely half a mile from the seal rookeries, to see which seals they might drive off to the killing pens; for the seals were driven like sheep, to be afterwards worked up into fur seal skins.

o: »Ho!« zvolal Pantalamon. »Pohleď!

t: Pantalamon stepped up to them, and the holušíks began to move, and Kerik turned them inward, into the heart of the land, and they did not even try to go back to their companions.

o: Kotík byl jediným, jenž kladl otázky, a nikdo z jeho soudruhů nedovedl mu říci ničeho, leda že muži odvádějí lachtany takto denně po šest až osm neděl každého roku.
t: Kotík was the only one who asked questions, and none of his companions could tell him anything, except that the men drove the seals off like this every day, six to eight weeks every year.

t: "I'll go after them," said Kotík, and his eyes nearly popped out of his head as he shuffled along behind the old ones.

t: "The white sea lion is coming after us," cried Pantalamon. "That's the first time a sea lion has come to the slaughterings on his own!"

t: "Hush! Don't look back!" Kerik warned him. "It's the spirit of old Zachar."

t: The slaughtering grounds were scarcely half an English mile away, but the herd needed a full hour to get there, for Kerik knew that if the sea lions went too fast they would tire, and then their hides would tear into pieces when they were flensed.

t: So they walked very slowly past the Lion's Ridge and around Webster's house, until they came to the salt works, which at that moment lay out of sight of the sea lions on the shore.

t: He thought he was at the end of the world, but the roaring of the sea lions' rookeries sounded toward him as loud as the rumble of a train in a tunnel.

o: Tu usedl Kerik na zem do mechu a vyndal těžké cínové hodinky, nechal stádo půl hodiny vychladnouti, a Kotík mohl slyšeti, jak s okraje jeho čepice kapou kapky mlžné rosy.
t: Here Kerik sat down on the ground in the moss and took out his heavy tin watch, let the herd cool off for half an hour, and Kotik could hear the drops of misty dew dripping from the edge of his cap.

o: Deset minut na to nepoznával Kotík více svých přátel, neboť jim byly kůže rozříznuty od nosu k zadním ploutvím, staženy a hozeny na zem na hromadu.
t: Ten minutes later Kotik no longer recognized any of his friends, for their hides had been cut from nose to hind flippers, drawn off, and thrown down on the ground in a heap.

t: He turned and ran off at a jog – a jackdaw can cover a short distance very fast – back toward the sea, and the young prince was seized from head to foot by horror.

t: "That is terrible," said the Otter, rearing up out of the water as a great wave washed over him, and by a screw-like stroke of his tail flippers he was brought quite upright, three inches from the jagged point of the rocks.

t: "Splendid diving for a yearling!" said the sea lion, who could appreciate a good swimming feat. t: Kit landed right next to the Sea Sorcerer, a huge, ugly, bloated, sluggish walrus from the North Pacific, with a thick neck and long tusks, who knew no rest even in his sleep – and was sleeping at that very moment, his hind flippers half on the land and half in the surf.

o: »Probuď se!« zahafal Kotík, neboť rackové tropili strašný hřmot.

t: "What's that?" asked the Sea Sorcerer, and struck his neighbour the walrus with his tusks and woke him with the blow, and that one struck his neighbour, and so on, and in a moment they were all up on their feet, gawking in every direction but the right one.

o: »Hi! To jsem já,« řekl Kotík a houpal se v příboji, vypadaje jako malý bílý chumáček.
t: "Hi! It's me," said Kit, bobbing in the surf, looking like a little white tuft.

t: "Well, well! Let them flay me!" said the Sea Sorcerer, and then they all stared at Kit as if they were looking at some company of sleepy lords on a heath.

t: Kit was not in the mood for listening to any talk of flaying – he had seen enough of that today.

t: So he called out: "Is there somewhere, some place where the walruses could go and where people don't come?"

t: Mollusk-eaters!" He knew the Sea Sorcerer had never caught so much as a little fish in all his life, and still he only rooted about among shells and tangleweed, though he behaved as if he were some terrible monster.

o: Buřňáci, rackové a mořské vlaštovky, mořské slípky, govrušky, jepatky a potáplice, jež ustavičně slídí, kde by si mohli dovoliti nějakou nezdvořilost, chopili se tohoto zvolání a tak – dle slov limmeršina – po dobrých pět minut nebyli byste slyšeli na Mrožím Ostrůvku ani výstřel z ručnice.
t: The boobies, gulls and terns, the coots, guillemots, jaegers and divers, who are always on the lookout for a place where they might indulge in some impropriety, took up this cry, and so – according to the limmer's words – for a good five minutes you would not have heard a gunshot on Walrus Island.

o: Všichni jeho obyvatelé ječeli a vřískali: »Žráči měkkýšů!
t: All its inhabitants shrieked and screamed: "Mollusk-eaters!

t: "Will you tell me, then?" asked Kit, all out of breath.

t: Kit swam back to Novastoshn, leaving the gulls to cry.

o: Řekli mu, že lidé vždy honili holušíky – patřilo to k dennímu životu – a že když nevidí rád ošklivé věci, neměl choditi k porážkovým ohradám.
t: They told him that people had always hunted the bachelors – it was part of everyday life – and that if he did not like to see ugly things, he should not go to the killing pens.

t: When old Sea Wolf heard of his nephew's adventures, he said to him: "It is your task to grow up and be a great sea lion, like your father, and to have your nesting place on the shore, and then they will leave you alone.

o: Za pět let budeš s to, abys bojoval sám za sebe.« Ano i mírná jeho Matka mu řekla: »Nezabráníš nikdy zabíjení.
t: In five years you will be one who must fight for himself." And his gentle Mother said to him as well: "You will never be able to prevent a killing.

o: Jdi a hraj si v moři, Kotíku.« A tak Kotík šel a tančil ohnivý tanec s velice těžkým srdéčkem.
t: Go and play in the sea, Kotik." And so Kotik went and danced his fiery dance with a very heavy heart.

o: Tohoto podzimu opustil břeh, jakmile mohl, a pustil se na cesty samoten, protože měl v kulovité své hlavě myšlenku.
t: That autumn he left the shore as soon as he could and set out on his journeys alone, because he had an idea in his round head.

o: Šel hledat Mořské Krávy, ač-li jsou v moři takoví tvorové, a chtěl vyhledat v moři tichý ostrov s dobrým pevným břehem, kde by mohli lachtani žiti a kde by k nim lidé nemohli.
t: He went to look for the Sea Cows, if such creatures exist in the sea, and he wanted to find in the sea a quiet island with a good, firm shore, where the sea lions could live and where no people could reach them.

o: A tak pátral a pátral samo-ten Tichým Oceánem od severu na jih, urážeje až tři stal mil za den a noc.
t: And so he searched and searched alone through the Silent Ocean from north to south, covering as much as three hundred miles by day and night.

o: Byl-li břeh dobrý a tvrdý, v pozadí s úbočím, na němž by si mohli lachtani hráti, byl vždy na obzoru kouř velrybářů, vyvářejících rybí tuk, a Kotík věděl, co to znamená.
t: If the shore was good and hard, with a slope behind it on which the sea lions could play, there was always on the horizon the smoke of whalers rendering down fish fat, and Kotik knew what that meant.

o: Anebo tam bylo patrno, že tam kdysi tuleni přicházeli, ale byli povražděni, a Kotík věděl, že kam jednou lidé přišli, přijdou opět.
t: Or it was evident that fur seals used to come there once, but they had been slaughtered, and Kotík knew that where people come once, they will come again.

o: Shodnul se se starým tupoocasým albatrosem a ten mu řekl, že ostrov Kerguelenský je tím nejlepším místem pro toho, kdo chce míti pokoj a klid, ale když tam Kotík přišel, byl by býval málem rozbit na kusy o šeredné černé skalní útesy ve hrozné chumelenici za blesku a hromu.
t: He agreed with the old stupid-necked albatross, who told him that Kerguelen Island was the very best place for anyone who wants peace and quiet, but when Kotík arrived, he would have been smashed to pieces on the shaggy black cliffs in a terrible blizzard of thunder and lightning.

o: A když přece se prodral příbojem, poznal, že i tam kdysi bylo lachtaní hnízdiště.
t: And when he did struggle through the surf, he learned that there had been seal rookeries there once as well.

o: A stejně tomu bylo i na všech jiných ostrovech, které navštívil.
t: And it was the same on all the other islands he visited.

o: Limmeršin jich vyjmenoval celou dlouhou řadu, a povídal, že Kotík ztrávil celých pět let hledáním, odpočívaje každoročně po čtyři měsíce na Novastošně, kde si jej holušíkové dobírali pro jeho fantastické ostrovy.
t: Limmer listed a whole long string of them and told him that Kotík had spent five full years searching, resting four months every year on Novastosna, where the seal people pestered him about his fantastic islands.

o: Přišel na Gallapagos, hrozné to suché místo na rovníku, kde byl málem upečen do smrti; přišel na ostrovy Georgijské, na Orkneye, na Smaragdový Ostrov, na Malý Ostrov Slavičí, na Qoughův Ostrov, na Ostrov Bouvetův, na Cros-sety, ano i na pramalounký ostrůvek na jihu od Mysu Dobré Naděje.
t: He came to the Galápagos, a frightfully dry place on the equator where he would have been baked to death; he came to the South Georgian Islands, to the Orkneys, to Emerald Island, to Little Gull Island, to Gough's Island, to Bouvet Island, to the Crozets, yes, and even to a tiny islet south of the Cape of Good Hope.

o: Ale všude vyprávěli rnu mořští obyvatelé tutéž historii.
t: But everywhere the sea people told him the same story.

o: Lachtani přišli kdysi na každý ostrov, ale lidé je všechny pobili.
t: The seals came once to every island, but people killed them all.

o: I když plul tisíce mil ven z Tichého Oceánu a přišel na místo zvané Mys Corientes – bylo to, když vracel se z Ostrovu Qoughova – nalezl na skále několik set zprašivělých lachtanů, a ti řekli mu, že lidé přicházejí i tam.
t: Even when he sailed thousands of miles out of the Pacific and reached a place called Cape Corrientes—it was as he was returning from Gough's Island—he found on the rocks several hundred mummified seals, and they told him that people come there too.

o: Pukalo mu nad tím málem srdce, a zaměřil okolo mysu Hornova zpět ke svým vlastním břehům; a na své cestě k severu přistál na ostrovu plném zelených stromů, kde našel starého tuleně.
t: His heart broke over that sorrow, and he turned around Cape Horn and made his way back to his own shores; and on his journey north he landed on an island full of green trees, where he found an old fur seal.

o: – Umíral již, a Kotík mu nachytal ryb a svěřil mu všechen svůj bol. »A teď,« řekl Kotík, »teď jdu zpět k Novastošně a poženou-li mne s holušíky k porážkové ohradě, bude mi to jedno.«.
t: – He was dying, and Kotick caught him fish and gave him all his pain. »And now,« said Kotick, »now I go back to Novastosha, and if they chase me with the sea-lions to the killing-yard, it will be all the same to me.«.

o: Starý tuleň řekl: »Zkus to ještě jednou.
t: The old seal said: »Try it once more.«

o: Jsem posledním z bývalého hnízdiště Masafuerského, a v dobách, kdy nás lidé vraždili po statisících, byla na pobřežích pověst, že jednou přijde od severu bílý lachtan a dovede lachtaní národ na klidné místo.
t: I am the last of the former breeding-ground of Masafuer, and in the days when men killed us by thousands there was a legend along the coasts that one day a white sea-lion would come from the north and lead the sea-lion people to a peaceful place.

o: Jsem stár a nedožiji se této podívané, ale jiní se dožijí.
t: I am old and shall not live to see this, but others will.

o: Zkus to ještě jednou.«.
t: Try it once more.«.

o: Kotík zježil svůj knír – a byl to velmi krásný knírek!
t: Kotick shook out his whiskers – and it was a very fine set of whiskers!

o: – a řekl: »Jsem jediný bílý lachtan, který se kdy zrodil na pobřežích, a jsem také jediný lachtan, ať bílý či černý, který kdy na to pomyslil, aby hledal nové ostrovy.« To mu nesmírně dodalo odvahy.
t: – and said: »I am the only white sea-lion that was ever born on these coasts, and I am also the only sea-lion, white or black, that ever thought of seeking out new islands.« That gave him enormous courage.

o: A když se toho léta vrátil na Novastošnu, prosila ho Matka, aby se oženil a usadil, neboť nebyl více holušíkem, ale zplna dorostlým mořským lapačem s kučeravou bílou hřívou na plecích, tak těžkým, tak velkým a tak statným jako jeho otec. »Dopřej mi ještě rok času,« odpověděl jí; »pamatuj, matko, že je to vždy sedmá vlna, jež se dostane nejdále na břeh.«.
t: And when in the summer he returned to Novastosha, Mother asked him to marry and settle down, for he was no longer a pup but a full-grown sea-lion hunter with a curly white mane on his shoulders, so heavy, so large and so stately as his father. »Give me one more year,« he answered her; »remember, mother, it is always the seventh wave that reaches farthest ashore.«.

o: Bylo to dosti zvláštní, že tu byl ještě jeden lachtan – lachtanice vlastně, jež si usmyslila, že odloží svatbu až na příští rok, a Kotík tančil s ní ohnivý tanec podél celého Lukannonského pobřeží té noci, nežli se vydal na svoji poslední výzkumnou cestu.
t: It was rather strange that there should be one more sea-lion there – a sea-lioness, in fact, who had made up her mind to put off her wedding until the following year, and that night Kotick danced a fiery dance with her along the whole Lukannon coast before he set out on his last journey of exploration.

o: Tentokráte ploval na* západ, jelikož přišel na stopu velikému hejnu plotic, a potřeboval alespoň sto liber ryb denně, aby se udržel při síle.
t: This time he sailed west, for he had come upon the track of a great shoal of herring, and he needed at least a hundred pounds of fish a day to keep up his strength.

o: Honil je, až se unavil, a pak se stočil a usnul ve brázdách vln hlubokého příboje, bijícího o Měděný Ostrov.
t: He chased them until he was tired, and then turned and slept in the troughs of the waves of the deep surf, which beat against the Copper Island.

o: Znal pobřeží dokonale, a proto, když kolem půlnoci cítil, že je lehce vržen na ložisko mořských trav a chaluh, řekl si: »Hm, příliv je dnes nějak prudký«, a obrátil se pod vodou, otevřel líně oči a protáhl se.
t: He knew the coast perfectly, and so, when about midnight he felt that he was lightly laid on a bed of sea grass and kelp, he said to himself: »Hm, the tide is rather strong tonight,« and he turned under the water, opened his lazy eyes and stretched himself.

o: V tom ale vyskočil jako kočka, neboť spatřil veliká zvířata, čenichající v mělké vodě a okusující těžké chumáče chaluh.
t: But there he sprang up like a cat, for he saw great beasts sniffing in the shallow water and biting at heavy bunches of kelp.

o: »U velkých vln Magellanských!« bručel si pod vousy, »Co je to za národ, u všech mořských hlubin?«.
t: »By the great Magellanic waves!« he muttered under his whiskers, »What sort of people are these, in all the deep seas?«.

o: Nebyli podobni mrožům, lvounům, tuleňům, medvědům, velrybám, žralokům, sepiím ani měkkýšům, ničemu, co kdy Kotík dřív viděl.
t: They were like no walruses, no sea-lions, no seals, no bears, no whales, no sharks, no cuttlefish and no molluscs – nothing that Kotick had ever seen before.

o: Byli asi dvacet nebo třicet stop dlouzí a místo zadních ploutvovitých noh měli lopatovitý ocas, který vyhlížel, jako by byl vystřižen z mokré vydělané kůže.
t: They were about twenty or thirty feet long, and instead of hind flippers they had a paddle-like tail which looked as if it had been cut out of wet dressed leather.

o: Jejich hlavy byly nejsměšnější věcí, jakou kdy kdo viděl.
t: Their heads were the funniest thing anyone had ever seen.

o: Houpali se na svých ocasech ve vodě a pásli se, kloníce se slavnostně druh druhu a mávali svými předními ploutvemi, jako tlustý člověk rameny.
t: They rocked on their tails in the water and grazed, bowing solemnly to one another and waving their fore-flippers like a fat man waving his shoulders.

o: »Ahm!« zakašlal Kotík. »Dobrou zábavu, pánové!« Velcí tvorové odpověděli tím, že se klaněli a mávali ploutvemi jako signálovými vlajkami.
t: »Ahem!« coughed Kotick. »Good sport, gentlemen!« The great creatures answered by bowing and waving their flippers like signal flags.

o: Když se začali znovu pást, viděl Kotík, že mají hoření ret rozštěpený na dvé, tak že ho mohou na stopu rozevříti a zase sevříti, držíce mezi oběma laloky celé otepi mořské trávy.
t: When they began to graze again, Kotick saw that they had their lips cleft in twain, so that they could open them wide to take a scent and close them again, holding whole sheaves of sea grass between the two flaps.

o: Cpali si potravu do tlam a kývali se slavnostně.
t: They crammed the food into their mouths and rocked solemnly.

o: »Jaké torohavné krmení,« pravil Kotík.
t: "What a beastly way to feed," said Kotík.

o: Klaněli se znovu a Kotík pozbýval trpělivosti. »Dobrá,« řekl. »Máte-li náhodou o nějaký zvláštní kloub ve svých předních ploutvích více, nemusíte se tím tak chlubit.
t: They bowed again, and Kotík lost his patience. "Fine," he said. "If by chance you happen to have some special joint in your front flippers, you needn't boast about it so much."

o: Vidím, že se umíte půvabně klanět, ale raději bych věděl, jak se jmenujete.« Rozštěpené pysky se pohybovaly a roztahovaly; skleněné zelené oči zíraly tupě, ale zvířata se neozvala.
t: "I see you know how to bow prettily, but I would rather know what you are called." The split lips moved and stretched; the glassy green eyes stared blankly, but the animals did not speak.

o: »Nu!« řekl si Kotík, »jste jedinými tvory, s nimiž jsem se setkal, kteří jsou šerednější než Mořský Čaroděj – a horších způsobův.«.
t: "Well!" Kotík said to himself, "you are the only creatures I have met who are more ragged-looking than the Sea Sorcerer—and worse-mannered."

o: Tu si mžikem vzpomněl, co mu vykřikoval buřňák, dokud byl malým jednoročákem na Mrožím Ostrůvku a překotil se radostí zpět do vody, neboť poznal, že konečně našel Mořské Krávy!
t: Here he suddenly remembered what the gannet had shouted at him back when he was a little one-year-old on Mroží Island, and he tumbled back into the water with joy, for he had realized that he had finally found the Sea Kings!

o: Pásly se dál, kývajíce se v mořské trávě, a Kotík vyptával se jich ve všech řečech, jaké jen na svých cestách pochytil, a Mořský Národ mluví skorém tolika nářečími, jako lidské bytosti.
t: They grazed on, swaying in the sea grass, and Kotík questioned them in all the tongues he had picked up on his travels, for the Sea People speak almost as many dialects as human beings do.

o: Ale Mořské Krávy neodpovídaly, poněvadž Mořská Kráva vůbec neumí mluvit.
t: But the Sea Cows did not answer, because a Sea Cow cannot speak at all.

o: Má v krku jen šest obratlů na místě řádných sedmi, a říká se v podmoří, že proto nemohou mluvit ani mezi sebou; ale má, jak již víme, zvláštní kloub v přední ploutvovité noze a kývajíc jí nahoru a dolů dorozumívá se jím jako jakýmsi neobratným telegrafem.
t: It has only six vertebrae in its neck instead of the proper seven, and it is said in the world below the water that this is why they cannot speak even among themselves; but, as we already know, it has a special joint in its front flipper-like foot, and by wagging it up and down it makes itself understood by it like some clumsy telegraph.

o: Když se rozednilo, ježil Kotík již hřívu a trpělivost jeho šla cestou, kam odcházejí mrtví krabi.
t: When it grew light, Kotík was already riding Hříva, and his patience was going the way dead crabs go.

o: Tu se začaly Mořské Krávy hýbati pomalu k severu, zastavujíce se chvílemi, aby odbývaly směšné kývavé porady, a Kotík je následoval, mluvě k sobě: »Zvířata tak blbá, jako tato, byla by dávno již vyhubena, kdyby nebyla našla nějakého bezpečného ostrova a co jest dobré pro Mořské Krávy, stačí také pro Mořského Lupiče.
t: Here the Sea Cows began to move slowly north, halting now and then to hold their ridiculous, swaying consultations, and the Seal followed them, muttering to himself: "Animals as stupid as these would long since have been wiped out, had they not found some safe island; and what is good for the Sea Cows is good enough for the Sea Thief too.

o: Vše jedno, jen bych rád, aby si trochu pospíšily!«.
t: All the same, I wish they would hurry up a little!"

o: Byla to únavná cesta pro Kotíka.
t: It was a tiresome journey for the Seal.

o: Stádo Mořských Krav nikdy neurazilo denně více než čtyřicet nebo padesát mil, v noci se zastavovalo, aby se napáslo, a drželo se stále těsně u břehu.
t: The herd of Sea Cows never covered more than forty or fifty miles a day; at night they stopped to feed, and they kept always close to the shore.

o: Kotík ploval kolem nich, nad nimi i pod nimi, ale nemohl je popohnati ani o míli.
t: The Seal swam around them, above them and beneath them, but could not push them on by so much as a mile.

o: Když postupovaly dále k severu, odbývaly své kývavé porady po každých několika hodinách, a Kotík si div neukousal knírův netrpělivostí.
t: As they moved further north, they held their swaying consultations every few hours, and the Seal nearly bit off his whiskers with impatience.

o: Konečně viděl, že sledují jakýsi vlažný proud, a tu začal o nich mít trochu lepší mínění.
t: At last he saw that they were following some lukewarm current, and then he began to think a little better of them.

o: Jedné noci pohroužily se do jasné vody – zapadly do ní jako kameny – a poprvé, co je znal, začaly plovati rychle.
t: One night they plunged into the clear water – they sank into it like stones – and for the first time, he knew, they began to swim fast.

o: Kotík ploval za nimi, divě se této rychlosti; nenapadloť mu ani ve snu, že by Mořské Krávy byly takovými plavci.
t: The Seal swam after them, astonished at this speed; it never occurred to him even in a dream that the Sea Cows could be such swimmers.

o: Mířily k pobřežnímu útesu, příkře spadajícímu v hlubinu a pohroužily se v temnou sluji na úpatí jeho, na dvacet sáhů pod mořem.
t: They made for a coastal cliff that dropped sheer into the depths, and plunged into the dark cavern at its foot, twenty fathoms below the sea.

o: Byla to dlouhá, dlouhá plavba, a Kotík se již začal dusit nedostatkem svěžího vzduchu, až konečně vypluly z temného tunelu, jímž jej vedly.
t: It was a long, long voyage, and Kotík had already begun to suffocate from the lack of fresh air, until at last they emerged from the dark tunnel through which it had led them.

o: »U mé srsti!« zvolal, když vyrazil v širý proud na druhém konci průplavu, oddychuje a funě. »To byl dlouhý ponor, ale stálo to za to!«.
t: "By my fur!" he cried when he burst out into the broad stream at the far end of the bore, panting and blowing. "That was a long dive, but it was worth it!".

o: Mořské Krávy se rozdělily a pásly se líně podél krajů nejkrásnějšího pobřeží, jaké kdy Kotík viděl.
t: The Sea Cows split up and grazed lazily along the edges of the most beautiful coast Kotík had ever seen.

o: Hladce omleté skály táhly se tu na míle, jako stvořeny pro lachtaní příbytky a za nimi skláněly se dále po souši tvrdé píščiny, kde bylo místo pro hry, a byly tu víry vodní, kde mohli lachtani provádět své tance, a dlouhá tráva tu byla, v níž se mohli válet, a pískové dyny, po nichž mohli lézt nahoru i dolů.
t: Smoothly worn rocks stretched here for miles, as if made for seal rookeries, and beyond them the hard sands sloped further inland, where there was room for play, and there were eddies of water where the seals could perform their dances, and long grass lay here in which they could roll about, and sand dunes up which they could climb and down which they could slide.

o: A nejkrásnější bylo, že Kotík poznal dle doteku vody, v němž se lachtan nikdy nemýlí, že tu dosud nikdy nebyli lidé.
t: And the most beautiful thing of all was that Kotík recognized from the feel of the water, in which seals never go wrong, that no people had ever been here before.

o: Přesvědčil se nejprve, je-li tu dobrý rybolov, a pak ploval podél pobřeží a počítal rozkošné nízké písčité ostrůvky, napolo skryté ve skvostné valící se mlze.
t: He first made sure whether there was good fishing here, and then swam along the coast, counting the charming low sandy islets, half hidden in the splendid rolling mist.

o: Na severní straně vbíhala daleko do moře řada útesův, mělčin a úskalí, které na šest mil daleko nepustily žádné lodi ku břehu.
t: On the northern side a row of reefs, shoals and cliffs ran far out into the sea, and for six miles they let no ship come near the shore.

o: Mezi ostrovy a pevninou tekl hluboký proud k výspám kolmo se sklánějícím, a někde pod nimi bylo ústí tunelu.
t: Between the islands and the mainland flowed a deep current toward the capes, perpendicular to the sloping shore, and somewhere beneath them was the mouth of the tunnel.

o: »Je to docela jako Novastošna, ale desetkrát lepší,« pravil Kotík. »Mořské Krávy jsou jistě moudřejší, než jsem si myslil.
t: "It's quite like Novastosna, but ten times better," said Kotík. "The Sea Cows are certainly wiser than I thought."

o: Lidé, i kdyby tu nějací byli, nemohou slézti dolů přes skaliska; a na písčinách u moře rozkotala by se každá loď na třísky.
t: People, even if there were any here, could not climb down over the rocks; and on the sands by the sea every ship would be smashed to pieces.

o: Je-li vůbec místo na moři bezpečné, je to zde.«.
t: If there is any place at sea that is safe, it is here.«.

o: Vzpomněl si na samičku lachtaní, kterou zanechal doma, a ač spěchal, aby se vrátil do Nova-stošny, zkoumal přec pečlivě nový kraj, aby mohl odpověděti na všechny otázky.
t: He remembered the female seal he had left at home, and although he hurried to get back to Nova Stošna, he examined the new country carefully, so that he might be able to answer all questions.

o: Pak se potopil a našed ústí tunelu, ploval jím úprkem k jihu.
t: Then he dived and, finding the mouth of the tunnel, swam through it southward.

o: Nikomu, kromě Mořské Krávy nebo lachtana, nemohlo ani ve snu napadnouti, že by tam takové místo bylo, a i Kotík, když se ohlédl zpět k útesům, stěží věřil, že byl tam dole pod nimi.
t: No one, except the Sea Cow or a seal, could have dreamed even in his sleep that such a place was there, and Kotik too, when he looked back at the cliffs, could scarcely believe that he had been down there beneath them.

o: Šest dní trvala mu cesta domů, ač neploval nijak zvolna; a když se dostal na břeh blíže Lvouního Hřbetu, byla první osoba, s kterou se setkal, ona lachtaní samička, která tu na něj čekala.
t: His journey home took six days, though he swam none too slowly; and when he reached the shore near the Sea Lion Ridge, the first being he met was the female seal, who was waiting there for him.

o: Viděla, jak mu oči září a poznala dle toho, že konečně našel svůj ostrov.
t: She saw how his eyes shone and recognized by that sign that he had finally found his island.

t: Well, Kotík never fasted for four months, as every large seal does year by year, and his swimming excursions over the open sea toughened him thoroughly, and, most important of all, he had never yet grappled with anyone.

t: His curly white mane bristled with rage, his eyes blazed, his great tusks gleamed; it was a splendid sight to behold him.

t: Old Sea Wolf, his father, saw him roaring and thrashing the old gray seals as if they were herrings, and scattering the young squids in all directions; and the Sea Wolf roared and shouted: «He may be a madman, but he is the best fighter on the whole coast!»

t: Kotík roared in reply, and old Sea Wolf rolled toward him with bristling whiskers, puffing like a locomotive, while Mother and the she-seal who was to become Kotík's wife curled up together and admired their masters.

t: It was a splendid fight, for the two of them fought as long as there was a single seal that dared to lift its head, and when they had all been vanquished, father and son paraded side by side, snapping their jaws, proudly up and down the shore.

o: V noci, když zakmitla a zazářila mlhou severní záře, vylezl Kotík na holou skálu a rozhlížeje se po zpustošených hnízdištích a pokousaných a krvácejících lachtanech, řekl: »Nu, teď jsem vám dal náležitě za vyučenou!«.
t: At night, when the northern lights flickered and blazed through the fog, Kotik climbed onto the bare rock and, looking over the ruined nesting grounds and the bitten and bleeding seals, said: "Well, now I have paid you back properly for what you taught me!"

t: After a week Kotik and his army (some ten thousand pups and old seals) set out north, to the Cave of the Sea Cows.

t: But when the following spring they all met together at the fishing in the Silent Sea, the seals told Kotik such tales of new coasts beyond the Cave of the Sea Cows that many seals left Novastosna again.

t: It did not happen all at once, however, for seals need a long time before they think a thing through; but year after year more and more seals departed from Novastosna, Lukannon, and the other nesting grounds, for the quiet, sheltered coast where Kotik lies through all the summer, each year larger, fatter, and stronger, while the "pups" play about him in the sea, where no man ever penetrates.
